The dataset contains 20,058 chess games with a strong majority (80.5%) being rated games. The vast majority of decisive games end via resignation (55.5%), followed by checkmate (31.5%). Timeouts account for 8.4% of games, while draws remain rare at 4.5%.

White vs. Black: The First-Move Advantage

10,001
White Wins (52.2%)
9,107
Black Wins (47.6%)

White Advantage

White wins 52.2% of decisive games (excluding draws), translating to a 4.6 percentage point advantage over black. This confirms the well-documented first-move advantage in chess, where white's initiative from the king's opening move provides a measurable statistical edge.

Critical Finding: White's advantage STRENGTHENS at higher rating levels. At beginner levels (below 1200), white actually loses more than it wins (35.7%). But at expert levels (2000+), white wins 66.2% of games. This suggests that at higher levels, players are better able to exploit and convert the theoretical first-move initiative.

White Win Rate by Time Control

Figure 3: White's advantage is consistent across time controls, ranging from 51.1% to 55.3%

Across all major time controls (bullet, blitz, and rapid), white maintains a consistent advantage between 51% and 55%. The 15+10 time control shows the highest white win rate at 55.3%, while 10+5 shows the lowest at 51.1%. This consistency suggests the first-move advantage is fundamental to chess rather than time-control dependent.

Victory Status by Rating Tier

Figure 6: Higher-rated players finish games via checkmate less frequently, with resignation becoming dominant

At lower levels (below 1400), 40.4% of games end in checkmate. At higher levels (1800+), this drops to just 21.2%, with resignation becoming the dominant end (63.5%). This reflects the ability of stronger players to recognize when a position is lost and resign rather than play out hopeless checkmates.

Notable Finding: Three of the top 12 openings show BLACK winning more than 55% of the time: Van't Kruijs Opening (58.9%), Sicilian Bowdler Attack (58.9%), and King's Pawn Game Leonardis (54.3%). These represent cases where black's counter-attack strategy effectively neutralizes white's first-move advantage.

Conversely, Nimzowitsch Defense (37.4% black win rate), Philidor Defense (40.3%), and King's Knight Opening (38.6%) show the strongest white advantages among common openings.

Bullet games (10+0, 8+0) show the longest average game lengths (62-68 turns), likely because players make quick moves even in lost positions. Rapid games with increments (15+15) are shorter (57 turns) as players have more time to find converting moves. The 15+10 time control shows the highest white win rate (55.3%) among major time controls.

Key Findings and Strategic Takeaways

1. White's First-Move Advantage is Real but Context-Dependent

  • White wins 52.2% of decisive games — a statistically significant 4.6 percentage point advantage
  • The advantage STRENGTHENS at higher levels: 35.7% at beginner level vs. 66.2% at expert level
  • This suggests that stronger players better exploit the theoretical initiative that comes with moving first

2. Rating Differentials Predict Outcomes with Moderate Strength (r = 0.239)

  • A 200+ rating gap gives the higher-rated player roughly an 80% win probability
  • Smaller gaps (0-100 points) only marginally shift probability (52-56%)
  • Individual game outcomes remain highly unpredictable — rating is a guide, not a guarantee

3. Opening Choice Matters — Some Openings Neutralize White's Advantage

  • Van't Kruijs Opening and Sicilian Bowdler Attack favor black (58.9% black win rate)
  • Nimzowitsch Defense heavily favors white (62.6% white win rate)
  • Players seeking to maximize win probability should consider counter-attack openings at lower levels

4. Game End Patterns Shift with Rating Level

  • Beginners: 40.4% checkmate rate — games often played to the full finish
  • Experts: Only 21.2% checkmate rate — resignation before checkmate becomes common (63.5%)
  • Timeout rates remain stable (~8-9%) across all levels

5. Time Control Does Not Meaningfully Alter White's Advantage

  • White maintains 51-55% win rate across all major time controls
  • Longer games with increments (15+10) show highest white win rate (55.3%)
  • Bullet chess (10+0) shows the most balanced outcomes (51.9% white win rate)
Summary for Coaches and Analysts: The data confirms that chess skill — as measured by rating — is the dominant predictor of game outcome. White's first-move advantage is real but modest, and becomes significant only at higher rating levels where players can better convert positional advantages. For training purposes, focusing on position conversion and endgame technique (evidenced by higher resignation rates at top levels) would yield the greatest improvement. At the same time, opening theory matters: choosing lines like the Nimzowitsch Defense or Philidor Defense provides white with the highest expected return, while counter-attack openings can neutralize black's positional disadvantage.
